summary: One intentional governed implementation phase (alias N16-5-F-5-TB-HELPER-IMPL, canonical phase 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.30R.5R.2.1R.1R.2R.1R.1R.1R.1.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1), the CPIPC-valid direct .1 child of the completed predecessor N16-5-F-5-TB-TRIO-IV (COMPLETE / INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, RESOLVED-TRIO VERIFIED). Implements the privileged-helper + HPAC-PAWA-HELPER/1.0 protocol FOUNDATION described by the phase authorization's 62 sections: closed HPAC-PAWA-HELPER/1.0 request/response schema; the closed 5-member operation vocabulary (admin_mutation, certification_write, certification_read, ceremony_entry, presentation_evidence_write) with explicit no-reflection dispatch; the closed 5-role certification family (hpac_lifecycle_terminator excluded); the REQUEST_RECEIVED..RESPONSE_EMITTED / RESULT_EMITTED / INDETERMINATE state machine with the MUTATION_ATTEMPT_STARTED no-auto-retry boundary; a replay/freshness ledger (fresh/consumed/duplicate_in_flight/expired/conflicting); an evidence stager implementing stage-before-mutate / finalize-after-commit / INDETERMINATE-on-post-commit-failure; a recursive no-authority-export scanner asserted on every dispatched response; conjunctive helper-provenance verification (regular-file, single-hard-link, owner, mode, no-symlink, complete-byte SHA-256) against one already-open O_NOFOLLOW descriptor; same-file-object anti-TOCTOU execution via /proc/self/fd re-exec on Linux, fail-closed (UnsupportedPlatformProfile) on macOS/other per HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-REQ-104 (a disclosed, not silently weakened, platform gap); a private one-shot AF_UNIX channel (0700 dir, 0600 socket, single accept); OS peer-credential authentication via Linux SO_PEERCRED / macOS getpeereid, never request-supplied identity; configured-agent exclusion wired to the existing, unmodified hpac_pawa_agent_exclusion resolver; and bounded per-operation handlers for all five closed operations against an injected NON_REAL in-memory ProtectedStoreFoundation. The closed 21-value pawa_failure_code vocabulary is re-stated verbatim (not duplicated) and independently asserted byte-for-byte equal to hpac_protected_admin_writer.PAWA_FAILURE_CODES. Three new src/pcae/core files created; zero existing production files modified; zero contracts/schemas/dependencies changed. Focused suite: 51 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (Linux-only exec test correctly skipped on this macOS host). Broader regression across all 124 pre-existing pawa/ppa/hpac test files plus the new suite: 219 failed / 6197 passed / 10 skipped, independently compared against a same-tree baseline with the new files moved aside (217 failed / 6148 passed / 9 skipped); the full FAILED-node diff (not a truncated sample) isolates exactly 3 gross new, individually root-caused, non-security point-in-time production-file-scope guard failures from three separate historical phases (none touching PAWA/PPA/HELPER security logic, RHAMP, Gate5, or packaging) plus one independently-confirmed pre-existing flake that happened to disappear. Zero attributable security regressions. Runtime Observed / observe / unavailable; 0 plugins / 0 capabilities; first governed runtime external effect ABSENT / UNREACHABLE. F-5-B2 BLOCKED PENDING HELPER IMPLEMENTATION IV + REMAINING MIGRATION SLICES; F-5 CERTIFICATION BLOCKED; N-16-5 NOT CLOSED; N-16-6 / N-16-7 OPEN / UNTOUCHED (N-16-7 strictly last). Recommended next (derived, NOT begun): a small N16-5-F-5-TB-HELPER-IMPL.1 scope-fence reconciliation phase (widening the three stale guard allowlists), then N16-5-F-5-TB-HELPER-IV (fresh independent verification). This phase begins neither.
